objections.claim: The RELEASE-ACCEPTANCE mechanism is self-referential or unanchored. If the content-addressed step-ledger record is committed in the tag target, its `release_commit` cannot equal that commit because adding the record changes the commit SHA. If it is committed later or stored out of tree, the approach specifies no immutable external locator/trust anchor from which the tag workflow obtains that exact record; consulting mutable main would violate the frozen content-address rule. Define a non-self-referential, externally anchored acceptance mechanism and test that the accepted SHA cannot be substituted.

Blocker 4 explicitly includes the absence of CI for Meta Ads MCP. The approach adds a manifest and hermetic tests but never wires those tests into a named required CI job; per-slice test execution does not protect later changes. Add permanent required-CI execution and a regression proving a failing Meta Ads test blocks the check.

The prose oracle does not cover every Node-version claim as required: `[Nn]ode(\.js)?` misses common forms such as `NODE 18+`, `NODE_VERSION=18`, and other casing or separator variants. Because the acceptance fixtures exercise only spellings already matched, the oracle can remain green with an unreconciled sub-22.12 claim. Broaden the capture rule and add escape-form negative fixtures.
